title: A tiny hash map
hints: Every operation starts the same way: `bucket_of(key)` picks the chain, and you walk that linked list comparing keys with `strcmp` (not `==`, which compares addresses).

`put` first searches the chain and overwrites the value if the key is there. Otherwise it `malloc`s an `Entry`, gives it a **copy** of the key (`strlen(key) + 1` bytes), pushes it on the front of the chain and bumps `size`.

`strmap_free` owns three kinds of allocation: for every entry in every bucket free the key copy, then the entry (save `next` first), and finally the map itself. If copying the key fails in `put`, free the half-built entry and return `false`.
